basis: The author of the book on key b held a University of Central Florida appointment during the period when the author of key a's 2007 review was identified with that institution. The matching name and overlapping appointment support one career.

evidence.says: The Naval Academy lists Tom McCarthy as a history professor with a Yale Ph.D. and author of Auto Mania: Cars, Consumers, and the Environment.
A Wayne State dissertation cites Tom McCarthy's Auto Mania and identifies The Road to Respect, Yale Ph.D. dissertation, 2001, as by the same author.

basis: The review credit places Tom McCarthy at the Naval Academy, whose faculty page identifies him as the author of Auto Mania. A dissertation citation explicitly credits that book and The Road to Respect to the same author.

evidence.says: William V. Hudon of Bloomsburg University wrote the 1992 Church History review of Italian Confraternities in the Sixteenth Century.
A 1996 Bloomsburg publication identifies history faculty member William Hudon as author of Marcello Cervini and Ecclesiastical Government in Tridentine Italy.

basis: The reviewer and the author of the book on the other key are identified with Bloomsburg University in overlapping years. The matching name, institution, and dates support one career.

evidence.says: Revolt in Palestine by Ahmad Hasan Joudah (1987) is a revision of the author's 1971 University of Michigan PhD thesis.
The repository attributes A History of the Movement of Shaykh Zahir al-Umar al-Zaydani to Ahmad Hasan Joudah.
The publisher identifies the author of Revolt in Palestine as Ahmad Hasan Joudah and lists his University of Michigan PhD in 1971.

basis: The book catalogue identifies the 1987 book as a revision of the author's 1971 Michigan dissertation. The repository identifies the dissertation title on the other key, and the publisher confirms the author's degree and year.

evidence.says: Wofford identifies Philip Racine with Piedmont Farmer and Seeing Spartanburg; he joined its faculty in 1969 after a master's at Emory.
A citation identifies Philip Racine's Atlanta's Schools as an Emory dissertation dated 1969.

basis: Wofford links the books on side a to its professor, but no source found connects him to the confiscation thesis on side b. A separate citation gives a different 1969 dissertation title, which warrants checking but does not establish that the keys represent different people.

evidence.says: David Bell lists Christopher Tozzi's Citizenship, Soldiering and Revolution as a 2013 Johns Hopkins dissertation.
Bell lists Christopher Tozzi's 2013 Johns Hopkins thesis as revised and published as Nationalizing France's Army in 2016.

basis: David Bell identifies the dissertation on key b and states that Tozzi's 2013 Johns Hopkins thesis was revised into the book on key a.

evidence.says: In 2009 Kevin Flatt was at Redeemer; his McMaster PhD dissertation was The Survival and Decline of the Evangelical Identity of the United Church of Canada, 1930–1971.
Redeemer lists Kevin Flatt's publications, including Theological Innovation from Spiritual Experience (2009) and Secularization Theory's Differentiation Problem (2023).

basis: The 2009 grant announcement identifies the dissertation author as a Redeemer historian, and Redeemer's faculty page lists works on the other key under Kevin Flatt. The shared institutional career links the two records.

evidence.says: Aaron Benanav's CV lists his 2015 UCLA thesis, A Global History of Unemployment, and his 2020 book, Automation and the Future of Work.

basis: Benanav's university-hosted CV identifies both the thesis on key b and the book on key a as his works.
